title: Span & Model-Call Tracing Cookbook for Tooling and Function Calls
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic cookbook for instrumenting spans across model calls, tool/function invocation, and multi-model fanouts. The goal is to make traces useful for: (1) fast incident investigation, (2) cost attribution for tool usage, and (3) quality regression debugging when model outputs differ after rollouts.

Scope and motivation:
- Why: model->tool->model cycles and function/tool-calling are common in chat and structured output flows. Current traces often collapse these calls or lose context (arguments, prompt snippets, chosen tool). That makes it hard to: identify which tool call introduced latency, which model variant produced a divergent answer, or whether KV cache evictions happened mid-flow.
- Audience: instrumentation engineers, SREs doing incident debugging, solutions engineers validating customer flows.

High-level tracing rules (opinionated):
1) Preserve human-readable context but limit size. Include short prompt hashes and truncated prompt fingerprints (first 512 chars) only when sampling low.
2) Parent-child mapping: every tool/function call must be an explicit child span of the model inference span that initiated it. If a model fanout spawns N downstream model calls, create a fanout root span with a field fanout.count=N.
3) Idempotent identifiers: include request_id, session_id (if available), and prompt_id in every span to allow session-based reconstruction without deep trace joins.
4) Sampling policy: prefer low-sampled traces for full prompt payload; high-rate synthetic probes should use minimal span attributes to avoid storage blowup.

Recommended span schema (flat key/value attributes, keep to ~20 keys):
- span.name: short identifier (e.g., model.generate, tool.call, model.embedding)
- span.type: inference | tool | embedding | routing
- telemetry.request_id: global request id (uuid)
- telemetry.session_id: session or user id (if available)
- telemetry.prompt_id: internal prompt fingerprint
- model.name: e.g., redwood/vicuna-13b-q4
- model.variant: quantized | fp16 | int8
- model.seq_len: integer
- tool.name: e.g., code-exec, web-search, calc
- tool.latency_ms: reported from the tool (if measured separately)
- fanout.index: index within model fanout (0..N)
- fanout.count: total spawned
- kvcache.warm: true | false
- sample.rate: effective trace sampling rate (e.g., 0.01)
- error.code: internal error code
- error.message: brief
- cost.tokens_in / cost.tokens_out: numeric strings (for later aggregation)

Span examples (textual):
- Model root span: span.name=model.generate; type=inference; contains telemetry.request_id, model.name, model.variant, telemetry.prompt_id, kvcache.warm, sample.rate.
- Tool call child: span.name=tool.call; type=tool; parent= model.generate; contains tool.name, tool.latency_ms, fanout.index (if part of fanout), linked_artifact (e.g., external request id).
- Fanout root (when single user request fans out to multiple models or multiple prompt prefixes): span.name=model.fanout; fanout.count=N; child spans model.generate#0, model.generate#1 etc.

Sampling heuristics:
- Full payload traces (prompt text + tool args) at 0.1% of production traffic by default (configurable per route). Use stored prompt hash in high-sample traces only.
- For all errors/exceptions, force-sample full trace (100%).
- Canary traffic: sample at 5-10% for the first week after rollout to catch quality regressions.
- Synthetic probes: sample headers-only traces; keep body suppressed.

Dashboard and investigation notes (practical widgets):
- Tool latency heatmap: x axis = tool.name, y axis = 50/90/99 quantiles, filterable by model.variant and tenant. Intent: find tools causing downstream tail latency.
- Fanout cost scatter: show fanout.count vs tokens_out and cost per request. Useful to detect regression where rollout causes more downstream calls.
- Prompt-fingerprint drift panel: track frequency of top 50 prompt hashes over time; sudden changes can signal UX or prompt engineering issues.
- Trace-linked error explorer: counts by error.code with link to representative sampled trace; automatically expand to show tool calls and kvcache.warm flag.
- Session-replay shortcut: for a given session_id show sequence of spans + top-level logs (if available).

Operator playbook (quick steps during an incident):
1) Query trace by telemetry.request_id or session_id in the incident time window (start with a small window + high QPS routes).
2) If trace sample missing, use prompt_id and fanout.count to reconstruct via logs/dashboard panels (fanout scatter helps).
3) Inspect child spans for tool.latency_ms or error.code. Use tool-latency heatmap to see if this is single-tenant or global.
4) Check kvcache.warm on model spans; if multiple cold cache flags appear concurrently, suspect cache eviction/rolling restart.
5) For regressions in output quality, pull canary vs prod traces and compare model.variant and model.seq_len distribution.

Instrumenting common SDKs (notes for implementers):
- JS/TS SDK: attach telemetry.request_id to headers: x-rw-request-id. Ensure model.generate wraps outgoing tool calls to create child spans using the tracing client.
- Python: provide a contextmanager (rw_tracing.model_span(...)) that automatically sets parent spans for any tool.call calls done while active.
- Go: explicit SpanFactory with helpers for fanout indices to avoid name collisions in parallel goroutines.

Operational constraints and cost control:
- Cap span attribute size: any string longer than 2048 chars should be truncated or stored as a reference id.
- TTL: raw trace retention policy should be tiered: full traces 14 days, compact metadata 90 days, aggregates indefinite.
- Cardinality: avoid high-cardinality keys where possible (user email, raw prompt). Use hashed IDs with friendly aliases in sampled traces.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-ups):
- Decide canonical field names for cost.* attributes and whether to include currency in trace (JIRA-OBS-889).
- Prototype a trace-enrichment service that can attach model eval metrics (per-prompt quality score) to sampled traces.
- Sampling configuration UI: knob suggestions and default per-route profiles.

Appendix: quick checklists
- From PR: instrumented endpoints must populate telemetry.request_id and telemetry.session_id (if available).
- From SRE: ensure synthetic probes have dedicated trace tags to exclude them from production SLO calculations.
- From product: tag rollout canary traces with deployment.id to make per-rollout comparisons easy.

References:
- see linked artifacts for trace spec and telemetry PR.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally prescriptive; aim is to reduce investigation time. Feedback: is the recommended ~20-attribute budget realistic for our current SDKs?
- If you have sample trace JSONs from real incidents that exercise tool chains, attach them to JIRA-OBS-882.
